summary: Defines MIB objects for managing the Operations, Administration, and Maintenance capabilities of Ethernet-like interfaces, following the OAM clauses of the Ethernet in the First Mile standards. It complements SNMP with link-specific functions. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Network cables need regular checkups. This note gives a standard list of questions an administrator's tool can ask about an Ethernet link's health.

questions: what is the ethernet oam mib
how to manage ethernet oam with snmp
subtitle: SNMP objects for the link-level health checks that Ethernet OAM adds to a single Ethernet link.

tldr.problem: The IEEE 802.3ah Ethernet in the First Mile work added Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) functions to Ethernet-like interfaces, but SNMP management tools had no standard way to control or read them.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4878 defines the DOT3-OAM-MIB module, with six groups of objects covering OAM control, the peer, loopback, frame statistics, event configuration and an event log, plus two notifications.
tldr.outcome: An SNMP manager can switch OAM on or off per interface, start remote loopback, tune error thresholds and learn about link events. The RFC warns that OAM itself has no authentication, so it suits protected links.

today: RFC 4878 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2007. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why an Ethernet OAM MIB
sections.content:
The IEEE 802.3ah Ethernet in the First Mile (EFM) taskforce added new management capabilities to Ethernet-like interfaces: discovery, error signaling, loopback and link monitoring. RFC 4878 defines the part of the Management Information Base (MIB) that lets SNMP-based tools manage them.

EFM was aimed at Ethernet access networks, with work on optics, copper and Ethernet passive optical networks as well as OAM. The RFC notes that Ethernet OAM can also run on Ethernet links that are not EFM.

The module is written in SMIv2 (RFC 2578, RFC 2579, RFC 2580). Its objects do not overlap with the Interfaces MIB or the Ethernet-like interfaces MIB, and they use the same ifIndex as the Ethernet interface they describe.
sections.eli5: Some new Ethernet cables can check on themselves. This note is the list of buttons and gauges that a network manager's program can use to talk to that feature.

sections.title: What Ethernet OAM Does
sections.content:
Ethernet OAM works at layer two between two directly connected Ethernet stations. That makes it complementary to SNMP, which needs layer three and above. SNMP can then be used to manage how one station's OAM interacts with its neighbor.

The mandatory core covers discovery (is the other end OAM capable, and which functions does it support), a state machine, and some critical event flows. There are three optional groups: link events, remote loopback, and variable retrieval and response. Each optional group is controlled by its own MIB table or tables.

  • Remote fault indication: one end signals that its receive path is not working. Some physical layers can run in unidirectional mode so that frames can still carry this signal.
  • Link monitoring: one end tells the other about important events, and can query the peer's interface variables.
  • Remote loopback: the peer echoes every received packet back without modification. This is intrusive, because the far end stops forwarding higher-layer traffic.

An OAM protocol data unit (OAMPDU) is a valid Ethernet frame sent to the reserved Slow Protocols MAC address, with the Slow Protocols type and the subtype reserved for Ethernet OAM.
sections.eli5: Two neighbors on the same string between two tin cans can check that they hear each other, tell each other about problems, and even repeat back everything they hear to test the string.

sections.title: How the MIB Is Organized
sections.content:
The objects are split into six groups, each built on a table indexed by ifIndex:

  • dot3OamTable: the primary controls and status, including the admin state, operational status, mode, maximum OAMPDU size, configuration revision and supported functions.
  • dot3OamPeerTable: what is known about the peer, such as its MAC address, vendor OUI, mode and supported functions.
  • dot3OamLoopbackTable: enabling and disabling loopback and reading its status.
  • dot3OamStatsTable: counts of OAM frames sent and received by type.
  • dot3OamEventConfigTable: which events produce notifications, through OAM and/or SNMP.
  • dot3OamEventLogTable: local and remote events detected through OAM.

Two notifications report events, one for threshold crossings and one for non-threshold events. The module sits at { mib-2 158 }. Section 4.3 maps every IEEE 802.3ah Clause 30 managed object to a MIB object here, and the RFC states that no 802.3ah managed object is left out.
sections.eli5: The list is organized into six drawers: settings, facts about the neighbor, the echo test, counters, which alarms to turn on, and a diary of what happened.

sections.title: Control, Discovery and Modes
sections.content:
dot3OamAdminState is enabled(1) or disabled(2) and always starts disabled until management action or retained configuration enables it. dot3OamMode is passive(1) or active(2). An active entity can start monitoring activities, for example by putting the remote entity into loopback; a passive one generally waits for the peer. The default should be active unless the system is known to take a subservient role.

dot3OamOperStatus reports how discovery is going. Its values are disabled, linkFault, passiveWait, activeSendLocal, sendLocalAndRemote, sendLocalAndRemoteOk, oamPeeringLocallyRejected, oamPeeringRemotelyRejected, operational and nonOperHalfDuplex. Either side may decline peering after seeing the other's configuration. Because OAM is not designed to work completely over half-duplex interfaces, nonOperHalfDuplex(10) is returned when OAM is enabled but the interface is half duplex.

dot3OamMaxOamPduSize is in the range 64 to 1518 octets, and peers negotiate the smaller of their two maxima. dot3OamFunctionsSupported is a bit string: unidirectionalSupport, loopbackSupport, eventSupport and variableSupport.
sections.eli5: Two kids meet and first work out whether both want to play and what games each knows. Only after both say yes can they start. One may be the leader who suggests games, and the other waits to be asked.

sections.title: Loopback, Statistics and Events
sections.content:
dot3OamLoopbackStatus can read noLoopback, initiatingLoopback, remoteLoopback, terminatingLoopback, localLoopback or unknown. Only initiatingLoopback and terminatingLoopback can be written. Writing initiatingLoopback starts the process only when the status is noLoopback, and writing terminatingLoopback only has an effect while in remoteLoopback. The dot3OamLoopbackIgnoreRx object controls whether the local station processes or ignores loopback commands received from a peer.

The statistics table counts OAMPDUs by kind in both directions: information, unique and duplicate event notifications, loopback control, variable request and response, organization specific, and unsupported codes. It also has a counter of frames lost due to OAM.

The event configuration table sets window and threshold values for four kinds of error events: symbol period, frame period, frame, and frame seconds summary. It also has enable flags for notifications, and for the dying gasp and critical event flags. Events land in the event log table.

The dot3OamThresholdEvent and dot3OamNonThresholdEvent notifications carry the fields of an event log row. They should not be sent more than once per second, and a manager should periodically check the event log to find missed events.
sections.eli5: The echo test is like shouting into a canyon to see whether your voice comes back, but while it runs nobody can use the line for anything else. The alarms ring only when too many mistakes happen in a short time.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Readable objects can reveal information about network traffic. The RFC is frank that, unlike SNMP, IEEE 802.3ah OAM has no encryption or authentication. It should be used where the interface information is not sensitive or where the facility terminations are protected. By default OAM is disabled on Ethernet-like interfaces, so it is not a risk until enabled.

In access networks, the customer-side device is typically configured in passive mode, which stops it from reaching functions and information on the provider side. OAM is a slow protocol with very limited bandwidth, so it does not harm data traffic.

Remote loopback is the disruptive part. Once enabled, the remote station sends all received traffic back except OAM traffic, which disrupts bridging, IP and SNMP over that link. That is why dot3OamLoopbackIgnoreRx exists.

The RFC also says to treat dot3OamAdminState and dot3OamMode as sensitive, and recommends SNMPv3 with its cryptographic authentication and privacy. Deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: The echo test is useful but can interrupt everyone on the line, so who may start it matters. Only trusted people should hold the controls, and the manager's own messages should be locked with a secret code.
